property_summary: For any address newOwner and any admin caller, after calling setOwner(newOwner) (by admin) the public owner getter equals the provided newOwner; the mutant that assigns admin to owner instead breaks this by making owner == admin for some newOwner != admin.

For any admin caller and any candidate address _owner, calling setOwner(_owner) by the admin updates the public owner getter to exactly _owner; the mutant that omits the assignment still returns true but does not update owner, violating this property for some fuzzed _owner values.

For any caller address provided to setOwner by the admin, the contract's public owner getter returns exactly that address after the call; the mutant instead sets owner to address(0) for some inputs and thus violates this guarantee.

For every caller allowed by onlyAdmin, after setOwner(_owner) completes the contract's owner equals the provided _owner; the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender so for some _owner (not equal to admin) this invariant is broken.

Rule: Only the original admin (the deployer stored in admin) can call setOwner successfully; the mutant that checks msg.sender == owner allows non-admins who become owner to call setOwner after ownership transfer and thus can change owner again — breaking the invariant that only the initial admin can perform admin-only actions.
For every caller and owner address, when the admin calls setOwner it completes successfully and returns true; the mutant breaks this by returning false for some inputs.

For all callers, only the admin (the deployer) can successfully call setOwner (call completes and returns true); the mutant that removes the admin check allows some non-admin caller to complete setOwner, violating this rule.

For all callers, only the original admin (the deployer) can successfully change owner via setOwner; the mutant that removes the onlyAdmin check allows some non-admin caller to change owner, breaking this rule.

For any caller address X and any new owner address Y, only the deployer-admin (the address that constructed C) can change owner via setOwner; the mutant that removes the onlyAdmin check allows non-admin callers to change owner, so there exist inputs (caller != admin) where owner differs.

For all callers and target owner addresses, only the deploying admin can successfully change C.owner via setOwner; the mutant that removes the onlyAdmin check allows a non-admin caller to change owner for some inputs (caller != admin and newOwner arbitrary).

For every caller address A and candidate new owner O, only the contract deployer (admin) can make setOwner succeed and change the public owner; the mutant removing the onlyAdmin check allows some non-admin caller A to successfully change owner to O, violating this property.
